```{r}
library(knitr)

hook_output <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("output")
knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) {
  lines <- options$output.lines
  if (is.null(lines)) {
    return(hook_output(x, options))  # pass to default hook
  }
  x <- unlist(strsplit(x, "\n"))
  more <- "..."
  if (length(lines)==1) {        # first n lines
    if (length(x) > lines) {
      # truncate the output, but add ....
      x <- c(head(x, lines), more)
    }
  } else {
    x <- c(more, x[lines], more)
  }
  # paste these lines together
  x <- paste(c(x, ""), collapse = "\n")
  hook_output(x, options)
})
ggplot2::theme_set(ggplot2::theme_bw(base_size = 16))
```

# Programming Topics

<h2> Benchmarking: comparing the speed of code </h2>
<h2> Profiling: finding the bottleneck </h2>
<h2> Object size, attributes, and equality </h2>
<h2> Finding source code: generics, primitives, compiled code </h2>
<h2> Rcpp, vectorization, and parallel computing </h2>

::: notes
- Rizzo Chapter 15. Theme: first make it correct, then find out where it is slow, then make that part fast.
:::

## "Premature Optimization Is the Root of All Evil"

::: instructions
1. **Correct first:** write clear code; test it against known answers.
2. **Measure:** benchmark alternatives, profile to find the bottleneck (usually one line).
3. **Improve the bottleneck:** vectorize, preallocate, use better algorithms/data structures, call compiled code, parallelize.
4. **Re-test** for correctness.
:::

Tools: `system.time()`, `microbenchmark`, `bench`, `Rprof()`, `profvis`, `object.size()`, `Rcpp`, `parallel`.

## Example 15.1: Benchmarking Ways to Generate a Sequence

```{r}
s1 <- 1:10; s2 <- seq(1, 10, 1); s3 <- seq.int(1, 10, 1)
str(data.frame(s1 = s1, s2 = s2, s3 = s3))            # integer vs double!
```

```{r}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("microbenchmark", quietly = TRUE)
#| fig-asp: 0.33
library(microbenchmark)
n <- 1000
mb <- microbenchmark(seq(1, n, 1), seq.int(1, n, 1), 1:n, times = 500)
print(mb, unit = "us")
autoplot(mb)                      # violin plot of the timings
```

## Example 15.2: Benchmarking Ways to Initialize a Vector

```{r}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("microbenchmark", quietly = TRUE)
n <- 100
mb2 <- microbenchmark(
  numeric = numeric(n) + 1,
  rep = rep(1, n),
  seq = seq(from = 1, to = 1, length = n),
  ones = matrix(1, nrow = n, ncol = 1),
  as.ones = as.matrix(rep(1, n)),
  times = 500)
print(mb2, unit = "us")
```

## Without Extra Packages: `system.time()` and Replication

```{r}
timeit <- function(expr, reps = 200) {
  e <- substitute(expr); pf <- parent.frame()
  system.time(for (i in 1:reps) eval(e, pf))[["elapsed"]] / reps * 1e6     # microseconds
}
x <- rnorm(1e5)
c(sum_loop = timeit({ s <- 0; for (xi in x) s <- s + xi }, 20), sum_vectorized = timeit(sum(x)))
```

## Preallocation and Vectorization

```{r}
grow <- function(n) { v <- c(); for (i in 1:n) v <- c(v, i^2); v }        # copies every time!
prealloc <- function(n) { v <- numeric(n); for (i in 1:n) v[i] <- i^2; v }
vectorized <- function(n) (1:n)^2
n <- 2e4
rbind(grow = system.time(grow(n)), prealloc = system.time(prealloc(n)), vectorized = system.time(vectorized(n)))[, 1:3]
identical(grow(100), vectorized(100))
```

::: tip
Growing an object inside a loop is $O(n^2)$. Preallocate, or better, vectorize.
:::

## Example 15.3: Timing Two Multivariate Normal Generators

```{r}
n <- 100; d <- 30; N <- 1000
set.seed(100); mu <- numeric(d); Sigma <- cov(matrix(rnorm(n * d), n, d))
rmvn_chol <- function(n, mu, Sigma) {
  Z <- matrix(rnorm(n * length(mu)), n); Z %*% chol(Sigma) + matrix(mu, n, length(mu), byrow = TRUE)
}
rbind(MASS_mvrnorm = system.time(for (i in 1:N) MASS::mvrnorm(n, mu, Sigma))[1:3],
      choleski     = system.time(for (i in 1:N) rmvn_chol(n, mu, Sigma))[1:3])
```

- Also: `mvtnorm::rmvnorm(n, mu, Sigma, method = "chol")`, `rbenchmark::benchmark()`.

## Example 15.4: Profiling with `Rprof`

Where does a function spend its time?

```{r}
slow_boot <- function(x, B = 2000) {
  out <- c()
  for (b in 1:B) {
    xs <- sample(x, replace = TRUE)
    out <- c(out, median(xs))                        # grows the vector
    tmp <- sort(xs); tmp <- rev(tmp)                 # useless work
  }
  sd(out)
}
pf <- tempfile()
Rprof(pf, interval = 0.005)
invisible(slow_boot(rnorm(500), B = 4000))
Rprof(NULL)
head(summaryRprof(pf)$by.total, 8)
```

- `profvis::profvis({ ... })` gives an interactive flame graph (Example 15.5).

## Example 15.6: Object Size

```{r}
x <- 1:1e6; y <- as.numeric(x); z <- as.character(1:1e4)
sapply(list(integer = x, double = y, chars = z, df = iris), function(o) format(object.size(o), units = "Kb"))
format(object.size(matrix(0, 1000, 1000)), units = "Mb")      # 8 bytes per double
```

::: question
Why is `1:1e6` stored with 4 bytes per element while `as.numeric(1:1e6)` needs 8? (And why might `object.size(1:1e6)` be tiny in recent R? ALTREP!)
:::

## Examples 15.7 - 15.8: Comparing Objects

```{r}
x <- c(a = 1, b = 2); y <- c(1, 2)
x == y                         # elementwise, ignores names
identical(x, y)                # attributes differ
all.equal(x, y)                # describes the difference
isTRUE(all.equal(unname(x), y))
attributes(x)
```

# Finding Source Code

## Example 15.9: Display the Code of an R Function

```{r}
sd
body(var)[[3]]                 # pieces of a function
formals(stats:::quantile.default)$type
```

- `RSiteSearch("bootstrap BCa")` (Example 15.10) searches help pages and mailing lists online.

## Examples 15.11 - 15.14: Generics and Methods

```{r}
print                           # a generic: UseMethod("print")
head(methods(print), 8)
methods(class = "boot")
getS3method("print", "density")
```

- Unexported functions: `stats:::print.density` or `getAnywhere("print.density")` (Example 15.13).

## Examples 15.15 - 15.16: `.Primitive`, `.Internal`, `.Call`

```{r}
sum                             # .Primitive: implemented in C, dispatched by the interpreter
exp
body(mean.default)[[length(body(mean.default))]]     # .Internal(mean(x))
body(stats:::fft)
```

- The C/Fortran source is in the R sources (e.g. `src/main/summary.c`); browse it on GitHub (`wch/r-source`).

# Rcpp

## Example 15.17: A First Rcpp Experiment

```{r}
library(Rcpp)
cppFunction("
double sumC(NumericVector x) {
  int n = x.size();
  double total = 0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) total += x[i];
  return total;
}")
x <- runif(1e6)
c(sumC = sumC(x), sum = sum(x))
```

- `cppFunction()` compiles, links, and loads the C++ function (Example 15.18). For larger code use a `.cpp` file and `sourceCpp()` (Example 15.19), or an R package with `src/` (deck 12).

## Loops in C++ Are Fast

A loop-heavy statistic: the **random walk Metropolis** sampler for a $N(0,1)$ target.

```{r}
cppFunction("
NumericVector rwMetropolisC(double sigma, double x0, int N) {
  NumericVector x(N); x[0] = x0;
  NumericVector u = runif(N);
  for (int i = 1; i < N; i++) {
    double y = R::rnorm(x[i - 1], sigma);
    if (u[i] <= exp(-0.5 * (y * y - x[i - 1] * x[i - 1]))) x[i] = y; else x[i] = x[i - 1];
  }
  return x;
}")
rwMetropolisR <- function(sigma, x0, N) {
  x <- numeric(N); x[1] <- x0; u <- runif(N)
  for (i in 2:N) { y <- rnorm(1, x[i - 1], sigma)
    x[i] <- if (u[i] <= exp(-0.5 * (y^2 - x[i - 1]^2))) y else x[i - 1] }
  x
}
set.seed(4750); N <- 2e5
rbind(R = system.time(xR <- rwMetropolisR(2, 0, N))[1:3], Cpp = system.time(xC <- rwMetropolisC(2, 0, N))[1:3])
c(mean(xC), var(xC))
```

## Example 15.20 - 15.21: A Data Example

```{r}
#| eval: !expr requireNamespace("Lahman", quietly = TRUE) && requireNamespace("microbenchmark", quietly = TRUE)
library(Lahman)
bat <- Batting[Batting$AB >= 300, c("H", "AB")]
cppFunction("NumericVector ratioC(NumericVector h, NumericVector ab) { return h / ab; }")
microbenchmark::microbenchmark(R = bat$H / bat$AB, Cpp = ratioC(bat$H, bat$AB), times = 200)
```

::: notes
- Vectorized R arithmetic is already C code underneath: Rcpp does not help here. Rcpp helps when the R version needs an explicit loop with dependence between iterations (like the Metropolis sampler).
:::

# Parallel Computing

## Embarrassingly Parallel Simulations

Monte Carlo and bootstrap replicates are independent: split them across cores.

```{r}
library(parallel)
ncores <- min(2, detectCores())
boot_med <- function(b, dat) median(sample(dat, replace = TRUE))
set.seed(4750); x <- rexp(200)
cl <- makeCluster(ncores)                       # works on Windows too (PSOCK)
clusterSetRNGStream(cl, iseed = 4750)           # reproducible parallel RNG streams
t_par <- system.time(r_par <- parSapply(cl, 1:20000, boot_med, dat = x))
stopCluster(cl)
t_ser <- system.time(r_ser <- sapply(1:20000, boot_med, dat = x))
rbind(serial = t_ser[1:3], parallel = t_par[1:3]); c(sd(r_ser), sd(r_par))
```

- On macOS/Linux: `mclapply(..., mc.cores = )` (forking). For reproducibility use `RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")` streams.
- Overhead matters: parallelize **coarse** tasks (thousands of replicates per worker), not single cheap calls.

## Python Supplement: Timing and Numba

```{.python}
import numpy as np, timeit
x = np.random.default_rng(4750).uniform(size=1_000_000)
print(timeit.timeit(lambda: sum(x), number=3))        # Python loop
print(timeit.timeit(lambda: x.sum(), number=3))       # vectorized C
# from numba import njit  -> @njit compiles loops to machine code (Python's Rcpp analogue)
```

## Summary

::: instructions
- Measure before optimizing: `system.time()`, `microbenchmark`, `Rprof`/`profvis`.
- Preallocate, vectorize, avoid growing objects; work with integers vs doubles knowingly.
- Compare objects with `identical()` / `all.equal()`.
- Read source code: print the function, `methods()`, `getS3method()`, `:::`, R sources for primitives.
- Rcpp for loops that cannot be vectorized; `parallel` for independent replicates.
:::
